accepted.name: Aider LLM Leaderboards (Polyglot)
accepted.owner: Aider open-source project (Paul Gauthier; community contributors)
accepted.measures: How well an LLM edits code to solve 225 hard Exercism exercises in 6 languages using aider edit formats (2 attempts, with test feedback).
accepted.last_update_seen: 2025-10-04 (data commit); page says last updated November 20, 2025
accepted.update_frequency: stale (no new rows for ~13 months)
accepted.reproducibility: Open benchmark code and exercises (aider repo + polyglot-benchmark), run commands and per-run stats published; contributors may submit runs.
accepted.independence: Vendor-independent open-source project; some rows contributed by community, none run by model vendors.
accepted.contamination_handling: None stated; Exercism exercises are public (hardest subset chosen).
accepted.respectability_rationale: Well-known, transparent and reproducible coding benchmark from an independent OSS project, but run by one maintainer/community and stale since Oct 2025 with no current frontier models.
accepted.verdict_reason: Transparent and widely cited, but stale (Oct 2025); historical reference only.

boards.data_date: data file last commit 2025-10-04; newest run 2025-10-03; page "last updated November 20, 2025"

accepted.name: ARC Prize Leaderboard (ARC-AGI-1/2/3)
accepted.owner: ARC Prize Foundation (nonprofit; Francois Chollet, Mike Knoop)
accepted.measures: Fluid intelligence / novel abstract-reasoning puzzles (ARC-AGI-1/2) and interactive agentic environments (ARC-AGI-3), with cost per task.
accepted.update_frequency: per model release (frequent)
accepted.reproducibility: Public eval sets and testing harness open-source; scores on Semi-Private set run by ARC Prize; costs reported; per-task results not on the page.
accepted.independence: Nonprofit, vendor-independent testing; labs get early access/verification but scores are run by ARC Prize on held-out data.
accepted.contamination_handling: Semi-private held-out task set (not public); private set for competition.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Nonprofit with published methodology, held-out semi-private sets, cost reporting and frequent verified testing; the reference benchmark for abstract reasoning.
accepted.verdict_reason: Gold-standard held-out reasoning benchmark with cost-efficiency data and current frontier coverage.

accepted.name: Artificial Analysis
accepted.owner: Artificial Analysis, Inc. (independent AI benchmarking company)
accepted.measures: Independently run LLM intelligence benchmarks (composite Intelligence Index v5.0 of 9 agentic/knowledge/science/coding evals) plus API price, output speed and latency.
accepted.last_update_seen: 2026-10-29 (newest model on board: Mistral Large 4, released 2026-10-29; Gemini 4 Carbon 2026-10-28; Intelligence Index v5.0 rolled out late Oct 2026)
accepted.update_frequency: continuous (new models evaluated within days of release; speed/latency are rolling live measurements; index re-versioned periodically)
accepted.reproducibility: Detailed public methodology (harnesses, repeats, pass@1, judge models, prompts); per-model scores shown; most eval sets private/held-out; no open per-item results; bulk data via keyed API, site payload partly encrypted.
accepted.independence: Vendor-independent: AA runs all evaluations itself on its own harness; some evals co-developed with partners (Cognition FrontierCode, Harvey, Zapier AutomationBench, HeyGen) and graded by vendor LLM judges (e.g. GPT-5.6 Luna). Business model/funding not stated on pages read.
accepted.contamination_handling: Private held-out sets (AA-Briefcase private set, AutomationBench private 657-task split, CritPt v2 hard private list, Harvey private tasks, Omniscience v1.1 dropped its public questions); saturated evals rotated out with each index version.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Most widely cited independent LLM benchmarker with a detailed published method, frequent updates and private held-out sets; data and harness not fully open and some evals partner-built/LLM-judged.
accepted.verdict_reason: Independent, current (v5.0, models to 2026-10-29), broad coverage incl. all requested Anthropic/OpenAI variants with effort settings.

accepted.name: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL) v4
accepted.owner: UC Berkeley Sky Computing Lab / Gorilla project (Shishir Patil et al.)
accepted.measures: Function/tool-calling accuracy: single-turn AST (live + non-live), multi-turn, agentic web search and memory, hallucination/relevance detection.
accepted.last_update_seen: 2026-04-12 (site label; newest model on board dated 2025-12-11)
accepted.update_frequency: irregular; effectively stale for 2026 frontier models
accepted.reproducibility: Open code and data (github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla, Apache-2.0), per-category scores; per-item results reproducible locally.
accepted.independence: Vendor-independent academic project; evaluations run by the BFCL team (some community-contributed model handlers).
accepted.contamination_handling: Public dataset; "live" split uses user-contributed real-world functions; no held-out private set stated.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Academic, fully open code/data, widely cited, clear weighted methodology; but updates have stalled and 2026 frontier models are absent.
accepted.verdict_reason: Strong method but stale: no 2026 frontier models on the board.

accepted.name: Design Arena
accepted.owner: Arcada Labs (Y Combinator S25 startup)
accepted.measures: Crowdsourced blind pairwise human votes on AI-generated designs (websites, apps, UI components, games, 3D, SVG, slides, plus image/video/audio arenas), aggregated into Bradley-Terry/Elo ratings.
accepted.update_frequency: continuous (ratings refreshed several times a day; ~1.9M votes)
accepted.reproducibility: Vote counts/win rates per model exposed via public JSON; prompts/system prompts published; raw votes not open; methodology page currently 404.
accepted.independence: Vendor-independent startup; vendors can test anonymous codename models before launch (like LMArena).
accepted.contamination_handling: Live crowdsourced prompts (no fixed test set); anonymous battles.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Large, current crowdsourced design arena with own data, but young company, limited method transparency (methodology page 404) and preference-only signal.
accepted.verdict_reason: Own large-scale crowdsourced votes, updated 2026-10-30; design-preference niche, limited method transparency.

accepted.name: Epoch AI Benchmarking Hub + Epoch Capabilities Index
accepted.owner: Epoch AI (independent nonprofit research institute)
accepted.measures: Runs its own evaluations (GPQA Diamond, FrontierMath, OTIS Mock AIME, SWE-bench Verified, SimpleQA Verified, games/puzzles) on frontier models and combines them with external results into the Epoch Capabilities Index.
accepted.update_frequency: continuous (new runs within days of model releases; data zip regenerated daily)
accepted.reproducibility: Open data (CC-BY CSV zip), Inspect-based harness, public per-run eval logs for many runs (logs.epoch.ai); ECI bootstrap samples published.
accepted.independence: Vendor-independent nonprofit; FrontierMath was commissioned/funded by OpenAI, which has access to much of the problem set except a held-out portion (known caveat). Otherwise Epoch runs evals itself via public APIs.
accepted.contamination_handling: FrontierMath private/held-out problems, new novel sets (Chess/Mystery puzzles generated programmatically, undisclosed game variant); public sets (GPQA, SWE-bench Verified, SimpleQA) not controlled.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Independent nonprofit research org, published methodology, open data and logs, frequent updates, held-out sets for its flagship math benchmark.
accepted.verdict_reason: Top independent evaluator with open data; only caveat is OpenAI funding/access for FrontierMath.

accepted.name: EQ-Bench (EQ-Bench 4/3, Creative Writing v3, Longform Writing)
accepted.owner: Sam Paech (independent researcher)
accepted.measures: LLM-judged emotional intelligence in multi-turn roleplay scenarios and creative / longform writing quality.
accepted.update_frequency: per notable model release (weeks)
accepted.reproducibility: Open-source code on GitHub (EQ-bench org), sample transcripts/outputs published per model; judged by LLMs (Claude/Gemini/GPT judges).
accepted.independence: Vendor-independent individual project; relies on frontier LLMs as judges (judge-bias analysis published for EQ-Bench 4).
accepted.contamination_handling: Novel scenarios/prompts; pairwise judging; no explicit held-out refresh stated.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Widely followed, open code and published transcripts with judge-bias analysis, but single-maintainer project and entirely LLM-judged (subjective constructs).
accepted.verdict_reason: Best available EQ/creative-writing signal with frontier coverage; LLM-judged by one maintainer, so low weight and category other.

accepted.name: EuroEval (formerly ScandEval)
accepted.owner: Alexandra Institute (Denmark, non-profit research & technology org), EuroEval open-source project led by Dan Saattrup Smart; EU-project collaborators
accepted.measures: Language-model performance across 30+ European languages (sentiment, NER, linguistic acceptability, reading comprehension, knowledge, common-sense; per-language and aggregate mean rank score).
accepted.update_frequency: continuous (several updates per week; new models added as released)
accepted.reproducibility: Open-source Python package (EuroEval/EuroEval on GitHub), open datasets and splits, bootstrap CIs, per-dataset scores published; anyone can reproduce with the package.
accepted.independence: Vendor-independent non-profit; evaluations run by the EuroEval team/community with the same harness for all models.
accepted.contamination_handling: Re-sampled fixed splits of public datasets; no private held-out set stated; public benchmarks (e.g. MMLU translations) may be contaminated.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Non-profit, published rigorous aggregation method with bootstrap CIs and significance-based tie ranks, open code/data, frequent updates and a dedicated Slovene board with current frontier models; contamination control is limited (public datasets, val splits for API models).
accepted.verdict_reason: Best current Slovene-specific and EU-multilingual leaderboard with frontier models (gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-*, Gemini 3.x, GLM-5.3), though Claude 5.x is missing.

accepted.name: Stanford HELM (Holistic Evaluation of Language Models)
accepted.owner: Stanford Center for Research on Foundation Models (CRFM)
accepted.measures: Standardized, reproducible multi-scenario evaluations of language models (capabilities, safety, multilingual, domain).
accepted.update_frequency: periodic releases; Capabilities stale since 2025-11
accepted.reproducibility: Fully open: open-source framework, all prompts, per-instance predictions and metrics published in the GCS bucket.
accepted.independence: Academic, vendor-independent; runs models itself via APIs (some compute/credits donated by providers).
accepted.contamination_handling: None specific; uses public benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, IFEval, WildBench, Omni-MATH) with standardized prompting.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Top academic method with fully open per-instance data, but the main Capabilities leaderboard is ~11 months stale and uses public, potentially contaminated benchmarks.
accepted.verdict_reason: Highly transparent academic source, but lags the frontier badly (no 2026-Q3/Q4 models); use for historical/open-model context.

accepted.name: Humanity's Last Exam (official, lastexam.ai)
accepted.owner: Center for AI Safety (nonprofit) + Scale AI (data vendor), with HLE Contributors Consortium
accepted.measures: Expert-written closed-ended academic questions at the frontier of human knowledge; HLE-Diamond is a cleaned 1,000-question subset (500 reasoning, 500 knowledge).
accepted.last_update_seen: 2026-09-22 (HLE-Diamond release post); home-page table dataset date 2025-04-03
accepted.update_frequency: sporadic snapshots (release posts); continuous numbers on Scale SEAL board
accepted.reproducibility: Open dataset (HF cais/hle, cais/hle-diamond), open eval code (github.com/centerforaisafety/hle), published in Nature (2026); private held-out set exists for original HLE.
accepted.independence: Co-run by CAIS (nonprofit) and Scale AI (vendor to labs; Meta stake). Results produced by the organisers, not self-reported by labs.
accepted.contamination_handling: Original HLE had a private held-out split; public questions widely available (Scale flags models evaluated after public release). HLE-Diamond is public on HF, so contamination risk grows over time; HLE-Rolling fork for corrections.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Peer-reviewed (Nature) benchmark with open data/code from a respected nonprofit, but official results are infrequent snapshots, co-run with a data vendor, and the dataset is public.
accepted.verdict_reason: Authoritative HLE-Diamond snapshot (2026-09-22) with high/max/tools splits; static, overlaps Scale board, public-set contamination risk.

accepted.name: Kagi LLM Benchmarking Project (Kagi Offline Benchmark)
accepted.owner: Kagi Inc. (search engine company; offers these LLMs in its paid Kagi Assistant)
accepted.measures: Accuracy on an unpublished, periodically revised set of 116 tool-free reasoning/coding/instruction-following/multilingual trick tasks.
accepted.last_update_seen: 2026-07-09 (GitHub commit of the page); task list revision 2026-02-13
accepted.update_frequency: per model release (irregular); no update since 2026-07-09 (~3.5 months stale)
accepted.reproducibility: Closed: tasks unpublished (only example questions shown), no per-item results, no code; aggregate table only.
accepted.independence: Not a model vendor; run by Kagi, which resells these models in its Assistant. Some runs via third-party inference providers (openrouter, together, nebius, fireworks, cerebras).
accepted.contamination_handling: Private/held-out unpublished tasks, revised over time (mostly harder); claims tasks are not in training data.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Credible independent private held-out set with good contamination resistance, but small (116 tasks), opaque scoring, provider-mixed runs, and stale since July 2026.
accepted.verdict_reason: Useful contamination-resistant signal but small, closed and stale; lacks current frontier models (Opus 5.5, GPT-6.x).

accepted.name: Lech Mazur LLM benchmarks
accepted.owner: Lech Mazur (independent researcher)
accepted.measures: Independent niche benchmarks: Extended NYT Connections (verbal associative reasoning), creative story writing (LLM-judged pairwise), adversarial multi-turn debate (LLM-judged BT ratings), plus older multi-agent/hallucination tests.
accepted.update_frequency: per model release (new frontier models added within days)
accepted.reproducibility: Method, prompts and many per-item outputs/judgments published on GitHub; full harness partly open; NYT puzzles public.
accepted.independence: Vendor-independent individual; writing and debate rely on LLM judges from vendor models (panels avoid own family where feasible).
accepted.contamination_handling: NYT: extra trick words + newest-100-puzzles check; writing/debate: generated content judged pairwise (no fixed answer key).
accepted.respectability_rationale: Widely cited, frequently updated independent benchmarks with documented method and open outputs; single-person project, narrow tasks and LLM-as-judge for writing/debate.
accepted.verdict_reason: Credible, transparent, current (Oct 2026) independent evals, but individual-run and niche/LLM-judged; weight lower in composite.

accepted.name: LiveBench
accepted.owner: LiveBench team (Abacus.AI with NYU, NVIDIA, UMD, USC and other academic co-authors)
accepted.measures: Contamination-limited LLM benchmark with objective ground-truth or deterministic grading; 2.0 adds long agentic, browser, research and design suites.
accepted.update_frequency: new question releases every few weeks/months; models added continuously
accepted.reproducibility: Open code (github.com/LiveBench/LiveBench) and per-release questions published with delay; 2.0 suites partly rubric-graded; single run per model.
accepted.independence: Run by Abacus.AI (which also lists its own Smaug models) with academic co-authors; vendor-independent of the frontier labs.
accepted.contamination_handling: Regularly refreshed questions from recent sources; newest questions held out until later release; frozen codebases for coding.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Peer-reviewed (ICLR 2025) method, open code, objective grading and question refresh; run by a company that also ranks its own models, and 2.0 includes single-run rubric-graded suites.
accepted.verdict_reason: Widely cited contamination-aware benchmark with open method and current frontier coverage.

accepted.name: LiveCodeBench
accepted.owner: UC Berkeley / MIT / Cornell researchers (Jain et al.)
accepted.measures: Code generation Pass@1 on competitive-programming problems collected continuously from LeetCode, AtCoder and Codeforces, filterable by problem release date.
accepted.update_frequency: stale (no updates since Aug 2025)
accepted.reproducibility: Open code (GitHub LiveCodeBench), open dataset on Hugging Face, per-problem results in the leaderboard JSON.
accepted.independence: Academic, vendor-independent; runs done by the authors.
accepted.contamination_handling: Problems tagged with release date; time-window slider and model release dates flag likely-contaminated models (rolling fresh problems).
accepted.respectability_rationale: Academic, open, contamination-aware design with per-problem data, but abandoned since Aug 2025 so it has no current frontier models.
accepted.verdict_reason: Strong method, but stale (mid-2025 models only); historical reference.

accepted.name: LMArena (Arena, formerly Chatbot Arena / LMSYS)
accepted.owner: Arena Intelligence Inc. (LMArena; spun out of UC Berkeley LMSYS)
accepted.measures: Crowd-sourced blind pairwise human preference votes between anonymous models (Bradley-Terry ratings); plus WebDev/Code and Agent arenas.
accepted.last_update_seen: 2026-10-28 (dataset publish date); site header "Oct 27, 2026"; HF dataset modified 2026-10-30
accepted.update_frequency: continuous (leaderboard re-published several times per week)
accepted.reproducibility: Historical leaderboard snapshots open (CC BY 4.0); periodic open releases of vote samples; rating code (FastChat) open; full live vote data not public.
accepted.independence: Independent company but venture-funded and works closely with labs (pre-release anonymous testing of vendor models; past critique of private-variant testing, "Leaderboard Illusion" 2025).
accepted.contamination_handling: Live fresh user prompts (no fixed test set), so contamination is not an issue; style control and frequency re-weighting adjust for biases; human preference may reward style/verbosity.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Most widely cited human-preference leaderboard, huge vote counts, published method and open snapshot data; but measures preference (style-sensitive) and has vendor-gaming concerns.
accepted.verdict_reason: Canonical human-preference signal with CIs and votes; keep in preference/coding/agentic categories, not as a pure capability measure.

accepted.name: MathArena
accepted.owner: SRI Lab, ETH Zurich and INSAIT (academic); supported by an Epoch AI grant
accepted.measures: LLM math reasoning on new, post-training-cutoff problems: research-level questions and false-statement detection built monthly from recent arXiv papers, Lean formalization, plus (deprecated) 2025-26 competitions.
accepted.update_frequency: continuous (monthly new problem batches; new models added within days)
accepted.reproducibility: Open evaluation code (github.com/eth-sri/matharena), datasets on Hugging Face (MathArena), per-problem raw model outputs viewable on site; peer-reviewed papers.
accepted.independence: Academic, vendor-independent; funded partly by Epoch AI grant.
accepted.contamination_handling: Uses newly released problems (monthly arXiv-derived batches, fresh competitions); flags models released after the competition (possible contamination).
accepted.respectability_rationale: Academic group with peer-reviewed method, open code/data and per-item outputs, frequent updates and explicit contamination controls.
accepted.verdict_reason: Academic, open, contamination-aware math evals with current frontier models (updated 2026-10-27).

accepted.name: METR Task-Completion Time Horizons
accepted.owner: METR (Model Evaluation & Threat Research), independent nonprofit
accepted.measures: Length of software/research tasks (in human-expert minutes) that AI agents complete with 50% / 80% reliability.
accepted.update_frequency: stale - page no longer actively updated (was per major model release)
accepted.reproducibility: Open analysis code (github.com/METR/eval-analysis-public), published per-model and per-task results (task_results_1_1.yaml); most task contents private.
accepted.independence: Independent nonprofit; runs evaluations itself, often with pre-deployment access arranged with labs (OpenAI, Anthropic). No vendor self-reported numbers.
accepted.contamination_handling: Mostly private, held-out task suite (HCAST/RE-Bench) not published to avoid training contamination.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Top-tier nonprofit methodology with open code and per-task data and private tasks, but the board is no longer maintained and saturates above ~16 h.
accepted.verdict_reason: Highly respected method but stale: newest model April 2026, no current frontier models.

accepted.name: OpenCompass CompassRank (CompassBench / CompassAcademic)
accepted.owner: Shanghai AI Laboratory (OpenCompass team; state-funded research lab that also develops InternLM/Intern models)
accepted.measures: CompassBench: private Chinese/English question set covering knowledge, reasoning, math and (agentic) coding; CompassAcademic: average of public benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, HLE, AIME2025, LiveCodeBench, IFEval).
accepted.update_frequency: quarterly editions (CompassBench); academic board irregular, stale since 2026-03
accepted.reproducibility: OpenCompass evaluation toolkit is open source (academic board reproducible via configs); CompassBench questions private, no per-item results.
accepted.independence: Run by Shanghai AI Lab (not a frontier-API vendor, but develops its own InternLM models; InternLM not on current CompassBench). Model selection curated, China-heavy.
accepted.contamination_handling: CompassBench uses a private self-built set refreshed per edition; academic board uses public sets (contamination-prone).
accepted.respectability_rationale: Credible established academic lab with open toolkit and private held-out CompassBench, but sparse coverage (15 models), quarterly lag (data 2 months old), opaque question set and some vendor affiliation via InternLM.
accepted.verdict_reason: Useful independent-ish China-side cross-check with frontier models (Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6-Sol, Kimi-K3), but small, quarterly and already missing Claude 5.5 / GPT-6.x.

accepted.name: OpenRouter Rankings (LLM Leaderboard by token usage)
accepted.owner: OpenRouter, Inc. (model routing marketplace; not a model vendor)
accepted.measures: Real-world usage: tokens processed per model variant through the OpenRouter API (daily/weekly/monthly windows).
accepted.update_frequency: daily
accepted.reproducibility: Aggregate data open (CC BY 4.0, JSON); raw traffic private; methodology described on page.
accepted.independence: Vendor-independent router, but sees only OpenRouter traffic (skewed to developers/agents, cheap & free models, apps opting in); marketplace has commercial ties to providers.
accepted.contamination_handling: n/a (usage measure, not a test)
accepted.respectability_rationale: Transparent, daily, open-licensed real usage data from a large independent router; but it measures popularity/cost-driven traffic on one platform, not quality.
accepted.verdict_reason: Good adoption/price signal; must not be mixed into quality scores (usage, platform-biased).

accepted.name: OSWorld-Verified
accepted.owner: XLANG Lab, The University of Hong Kong (with collaborators)
accepted.measures: Success rate of multimodal agents completing 361 real computer tasks (Ubuntu desktop apps, browser, office, multi-app) in VMs.
accepted.last_update_seen: 2026-08-01 (newest verified run in data file; repo pushed 2026-08-07)
accepted.update_frequency: continuous, on verified submissions
accepted.reproducibility: Open benchmark code (github.com/xlang-ai/OSWorld), public tasks/evaluators, verified trajectories on Hugging Face (xlangai/ubuntu_osworld_verified_trajs), per-app breakdown.
accepted.independence: Academic; submissions are verified/re-checked by the OSWorld team; many submissions originate from model/agent developers.
accepted.contamination_handling: Public test set; fixed community-reported examples (Verified revision 2025-07-28); no held-out set.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Leading academic computer-use benchmark with open code, verified runs and published trajectories; public tasks and patchy coverage of OpenAI/Google models limit it.
accepted.verdict_reason: Academic, verified, current to Aug 2026 for Anthropic/Meta/Chinese frontier models.

accepted.name: Scale AI SEAL / Scale Labs Leaderboards
accepted.owner: Scale AI (Scale Labs research team; Scale is a data/RLHF vendor to frontier labs, Meta holds a large stake)
accepted.measures: Expert-built, mostly private benchmarks across frontier reasoning (HLE-Diamond), agentic coding/tool use (SWE-Bench Pro, SWE Atlas, MCP Atlas, RLI, HiL-Bench), professional reasoning, multimodal/audio and safety.
accepted.update_frequency: continuous (per model release)
accepted.reproducibility: Methods/papers published per benchmark; many sets private or partially public (e.g. SWE-Bench Pro public split, FORTRESS public split, DistressBench 50/50 split); no per-item results for private sets.
accepted.independence: NOT vendor-independent: Scale sells training data/evaluation services to the labs it ranks (incl. OpenAI, Google, Anthropic historically) and Meta owns a large minority stake; Meta (Muse) models top several boards. Scale runs evals itself; models must be evaluated the first time an org sees the prompts.
accepted.contamination_handling: Private held-out prompt sets on most boards; explicit contamination warnings for models evaluated after public release (HLE, MASK); public/private splits to detect overfitting.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Strong expert-built private benchmarks with published methods and frequent updates, but run by a data vendor with commercial ties to (and Meta ownership stake from) ranked labs; limited data openness.
accepted.verdict_reason: Valuable private expert benchmarks, but vendor conflict of interest (Scale/Meta) and closed data; weight accordingly.

accepted.name: SimpleBench
accepted.owner: SimpleBench Team (Philip of AI Explained YouTube channel and collaborators); tied to LM Council app
accepted.measures: Multiple-choice trick/common-sense questions (spatio-temporal, social, linguistic adversarial) where non-expert humans beat models.
accepted.update_frequency: per notable model release (irregular, weeks)
accepted.reproducibility: Code and 10-question public sample open; ~200-question main set private; AVG@5 at temperature 0.7; no per-item results.
accepted.independence: Vendor-independent individual-run project; the team also runs the LM Council app (commercial).
accepted.contamination_handling: Private held-out question set (only a small public sample).
accepted.respectability_rationale: Private held-out set and simple transparent scoring, widely cited, but small (~200 items, 9-person human baseline), run by an individual team with limited methodology documentation and irregular updates.
accepted.verdict_reason: Useful contamination-resistant common-sense reasoning signal, but small private set from an individual project; weight lightly.

accepted.name: SloBench (Slovenian NLP Benchmark)
accepted.owner: CJVT / University of Ljubljana (FRI) with CLARIN.SI; proposed by S. Zitnik, M. Robnik-Sikonja, S. Krek; supported 2025-2028 by LLMs4EU WP5
accepted.measures: Slovene-language NLP tasks (translated SuperGLUE, NLI, dialect COPA, pragmatics, MT, NER) scored by the platform on hidden-label test sets from user-submitted predictions.
accepted.update_frequency: continuous open submissions; frontier-model coverage sporadic and stale
accepted.reproducibility: Open evaluation scripts (docker); test inputs public, labels withheld; submitted systems optionally open (Verified tag only for reproducible open code); per-task sub-metrics shown.
accepted.independence: Academic, vendor-independent platform; results are self-submitted by researchers/community (mostly unverified), not run by SloBench itself.
accepted.contamination_handling: Hidden test labels plus submission rate limits; translated public benchmarks (e.g. SuperGLUE) may be contaminated via the English originals.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Authoritative academic Slovenian benchmark with open eval code and hidden labels, but results are self-submitted/unverified and frontier coverage is stale (newest closed models GPT-5 / Gemini 2.5 / Claude Haiku 4.5 on one board only).
accepted.verdict_reason: Best Slovene-specific signal, but no current frontier models (Claude 5.x, GPT-6.x, Gemini 3+); use for Slovene open/local models and historical context.

accepted.name: Slovenska pogovorna arena / Slovenian Chat Arena
accepted.owner: CJVT (Centre for Language Resources and Technologies) and Faculty of Computer and Information Science, University of Ljubljana; funded by Slovenian Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation + EU NextGenerationEU (PoVeJMo programme)
accepted.measures: Blind pairwise human preference of chatbot answers to Slovene prompts by Slovene users, aggregated with a Bradley-Terry model.
accepted.update_frequency: continuous (live votes); model roster changes irregularly
accepted.reproducibility: Method described (Bradley-Terry, 1,000 bootstrap resamples, ties = half win); vote data not published as a download; preference data used to build GaMS datasets; cited thesis Petric (2025).
accepted.independence: Academic; the same group (CJVT / UL FRI) develops the GaMS models that compete on the arena (potential conflict of interest, though votes are blind).
accepted.contamination_handling: Not applicable (live user prompts, blind votes).
accepted.respectability_rationale: Credible academic Slovene-specific human-preference arena with sound BT/bootstrap method, but tiny vote counts (only 6 models with >=30 votes, wide CIs), no Claude models, and run by the GaMS developers.
accepted.verdict_reason: Only live Slovene human-preference signal with some current frontier models, but statistically thin and missing Claude/GPT-6; use as a weak Slovene-quality indicator.

accepted.name: Snorkel AI Leaderboards
accepted.owner: Snorkel AI, Inc. (AI data-development company; supplies expert data to frontier labs)
accepted.measures: Own expert-built agentic benchmarks in enterprise environments (finance, insurance underwriting, manufacturing, RevOps, legal, workplace deliverables) and agentic coding, plus an economically weighted Digital Work Index.
accepted.update_frequency: per model release (frontier models added within ~2 weeks; exports dated 2026-10-20)
accepted.reproducibility: Proprietary/private datasets; per-benchmark methodology descriptions, Pass@1/Pass@5 and cost published; no open per-item data for enterprise sets.
accepted.independence: Not a model vendor, but sells training data/environments to frontier labs (potential conflict of interest); runs evaluations itself.
accepted.contamination_handling: Private held-out expert-built environments (not publicly released).
accepted.respectability_rationale: Own, current, documented agentic evaluations with costs, but proprietary data, small model set (16) and a commercial data vendor to the labs being ranked.
accepted.verdict_reason: Own current private enterprise/agentic evals (as_of 2026-10-20), but commercial data-vendor owner, closed data, only 16 models.

accepted.name: SWE-bench (official leaderboards)
accepted.owner: SWE-bench team (Princeton / Stanford; John Yang, Carlos Jimenez, Ofir Press et al.)
accepted.measures: Resolution rate of real GitHub issues in Python (Verified, 500 human-validated) and 9 other programming languages (Multilingual), judged by repo unit tests.
accepted.update_frequency: per submission; effectively stale since Feb 2026 (only Gemini 3.5 Flash added Sep 2026)
accepted.reproducibility: Open dataset, open harness, open mini-SWE-agent scaffold; per-instance results, logs and trajectories public in SWE-bench/experiments.
accepted.independence: Academic, vendor-independent; bash-only runs executed by the SWE-bench team, other rows are self-submitted by agent vendors (checked flag marks verified ones).
accepted.contamination_handling: None beyond human validation; tasks from public pre-2024 GitHub repos, so training-data contamination is plausible.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Gold-standard academic coding-agent benchmark with fully open data/code and an apples-to-apples bash-only board, but stale for Oct 2026 frontier models, saturating, and with known contamination risk.
accepted.verdict_reason: Highly reputable and open, but no 2026-H2 frontier models; use mainly as historical/second-tier reference.

accepted.name: SWE-rebench
accepted.owner: Nebius (AI R&D team)
accepted.measures: Resolved rate of LLMs on continuously refreshed, decontaminated real-world GitHub issue tasks with one fixed minimal ReAct scaffold, 5 runs per task.
accepted.last_update_seen: 2026-07-28 (HF data lastModified); newest model Opus 5 released 2026-07-24; news log last entry 2026-07-01
accepted.update_frequency: monthly-ish task refresh and model additions (last ~3 months quiet)
accepted.reproducibility: Open tasks on Hugging Face (nebius/SWE-rebench-leaderboard), Docker images public, paper arXiv 2505.20411; fixed scaffold and prompts documented; trajectories inspectable.
accepted.independence: Run centrally by Nebius (a cloud/inference provider, not a frontier-model vendor); same scaffold for all models; agent rows are reference evaluations.
accepted.contamination_handling: Rolling fresh tasks with creation dates; time-window selection; models released after window start flagged as potential contamination.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Rigorous model-focused method (fixed scaffold, multi-run averages with SEM, rolling decontaminated tasks, open data), run by an industry lab rather than academia; currently lags the newest Sep-Oct 2026 releases.
accepted.verdict_reason: Contamination-aware, apples-to-apples coding benchmark with open data; covers models up to July 2026.

accepted.name: tau-bench / tau2-bench / tau3 (Sierra)
accepted.owner: Sierra Research (Sierra Technologies, agent-platform company; not an LLM vendor)
accepted.measures: Customer-service agent reliability: tool use + policy following in dialogue with a simulated user (retail, airline, telecom, banking knowledge; pass^k).
accepted.update_frequency: per model release batches (Sierra-run) + external submissions
accepted.reproducibility: Open code (github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench), public tasks, trajectories published on S3 for most current submissions.
accepted.independence: Current boards run by Sierra itself; legacy entries include vendor self-reported numbers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Moonshot, Qwen, DeepSeek) flagged unverified.
accepted.contamination_handling: Public tasks; tau3 task fixes; no private held-out split stated.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Established, widely used agent benchmark with open code, published papers and trajectories; verification flags; but core tau2 board covers few current models and user simulator is an OpenAI model.
accepted.verdict_reason: Open, verified Sierra-run results; use tau3-Banking for current frontier, tau2 domains for early-2026 models.

accepted.name: Terminal-Bench
accepted.owner: Stanford University + Laude Institute (Harbor framework)
accepted.measures: Ability of AI agents to complete hard, realistic tasks end-to-end in a sandboxed terminal environment, verified by task tests.
accepted.update_frequency: continuous (new rows per model release; versioned task set)
accepted.reproducibility: Open tasks on GitHub/Harbor Hub (harbor run -d terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0), open task triage; leaderboard trial data stored on Harbor Hub; CI95 and pass@k reported.
accepted.independence: Academic/nonprofit-run; leaderboard compute partly funded by vendor grants (OpenAI, Anthropic, Z.ai, SpaceX AI); most rows use vendor-built agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build).
accepted.contamination_handling: Canary GUID, saturated/public-solution tasks removed, task set refreshed per version; tasks themselves are public.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Academic/nonprofit benchmark with open tasks and methodology, current Oct 2026 frontier coverage, CIs, continuous maintenance; caveat: scores mix model with vendor scaffold.
accepted.verdict_reason: Current, open, well-maintained agentic benchmark with frontier models and confidence intervals.

accepted.name: Toolathlon (Tool Decathlon) - Toolathlon-Verified
accepted.owner: HKUST NLP group (Hong Kong University of Science and Technology) and collaborators
accepted.measures: Pass rate of language agents on 108 long-horizon, multi-app tasks using 32 real MCP servers (604 tools) plus local toolkits, with execution-based evaluation.
accepted.update_frequency: per model release (team-evaluated), roughly monthly
accepted.reproducibility: Open code (github.com/hkust-nlp/Toolathlon), trajectories on Hugging Face (hkust-nlp/Toolathlon-Verified_Trajectories), 3-run pass@1 with spread.
accepted.independence: Academic; current board entries all independently evaluated by the team with the default agent scaffold.
accepted.contamination_handling: Public tasks with execution-based checkers and realistic initial states; no private split stated.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Academic, open code and trajectories, uniform team-run harness with multiple runs; new (Verified series since 2026-06) and missing several frontier models.
accepted.verdict_reason: Independent, uniform tool-use/MCP agent benchmark current to Aug 2026.

accepted.name: Vals AI
accepted.owner: Vals AI, Inc. (independent evaluation company, US)
accepted.measures: Independent evaluations of LLMs/agents on ~40-55 industry benchmarks (finance, legal, tax, healthcare, coding, science, math), mostly private datasets, plus composite Vals Index.
accepted.update_frequency: continuous (new models evaluated within days of release; Vals Index updated 2026-10-29)
accepted.reproducibility: Private test sets for most industry benchmarks (not reproducible externally); some public benchmarks and public trajectories; per-model cost/latency/tokens published; partial per-task breakdowns.
accepted.independence: Independent company running its own evaluations; some benchmarks built with industry partners; some rubric grading uses vendor LLM judges (e.g. EMB v1.1 judged by GPT-6 Luna).
accepted.contamination_handling: Mostly private/held-out datasets (dataset_type=private) to prevent training contamination.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Established independent evaluator with published methodology, own runs on private domain datasets, frequent updates and stderr reported; data/code mostly closed and LLM-judge grading on some tasks.
accepted.verdict_reason: Own independent evaluations on private professional-domain benchmarks, current frontier models, updated 2026-10-29.

accepted.name: Vectara Hallucination Leaderboard (HHEM-2.3)
accepted.owner: Vectara Inc. (RAG platform company, not an LLM vendor)
accepted.measures: Hallucination rate of LLMs when summarizing ~7,700 documents, judged by Vectara's HHEM-2.3 factual-consistency model.
accepted.update_frequency: frequent (roughly per new model releases)
accepted.reproducibility: Prompt published; dataset private; judge HHEM-2.3 is commercial (open variant HHEM-2.1-Open differs); no per-item outputs.
accepted.independence: Independent of LLM vendors; single commercial judge model owned by Vectara.
accepted.contamination_handling: Private (non-public) document set to avoid overfitting.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Long-running, frequently updated and widely cited, private test set; but narrow task (summarization faithfulness), closed proprietary judge, no per-item data.
accepted.verdict_reason: Current and useful grounded-hallucination signal, but single closed judge and narrow summarization task.

accepted.name: Vending-Bench 2 (Andon Labs)
accepted.owner: Andon Labs (independent AI-safety/evals company)
accepted.measures: Long-horizon agent coherence: running a simulated vending-machine business for a year via tools; score = final bank balance (start $500).
accepted.last_update_seen: not dated on page; includes Gemini 4 Carbon/Argon, Claude Opus 5.5/Sonnet 5.5/Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Sol/Astra, GPT-6.1 Terra (fetched 2026-10-30)
accepted.update_frequency: per frontier model release
accepted.reproducibility: Method described (VB1 paper + VB2 page); environment/code not public; per-run time series published on page.
accepted.independence: Vendor-independent evaluator; runs all models itself; has research collaborations with labs (e.g. Anthropic Project Vend) - minor caveat.
accepted.contamination_handling: Simulation-based, not a static Q&A set; not applicable/none stated.
accepted.respectability_rationale: Established independent evaluator widely cited in frontier model cards, consistent harness and multiple runs with SEM; environment closed and high run-to-run variance.
accepted.verdict_reason: Current frontier coverage incl. most scope models; independent, multi-run, published method.

source_meta.name: Official vendor price lists
source_meta.owner: Each model vendor (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, DeepSeek, Mistral AI, Moonshot AI, Zhipu AI, Alibaba Cloud, MiniMax)

source_meta.update_frequency: per model release / vendor price change

price_source.notes: All prices read from official vendor pages via curl (raw HTML -> text; OpenAI and xAI via their .md doc versions; Kimi table from the page's embedded JSX row data). USD per 1M tokens, standard/real-time tier, no batch or cache discounts. Where a vendor tiers by prompt length the lowest tier is recorded and the threshold noted (OpenAI <=272K, Gemini Pro <=200k, xAI <200k, Claude Haiku 5.5 <=100k, Qwen plus <=256K, MiniMax <=512k). DeepSeek has peak/off-peak pricing: PEAK (full) price recorded. Time-limited prices (Gemini 4 Argon until 2026-11-30, Gemini 3.8/3.6 Flash until 2026-12-31, GPT-5.6 Sol promo) are recorded as currently charged with the scheduled price in notes. MiniMax-M3 recorded at the effective 'permanent 50% off' price; qwen3.7-plus at list price (discount figure not shown). OpenRouter public /models used only as a cross-check (matches official for Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.5, Fable 5.1, gpt-6.x, Gemini 4 Argon, grok-4.7, Kimi K3.1 Pro, MiniMax-M3, Mistral Large 4, qwen3.8-max). openai.com/api/pricing now shows ChatGPT business plans, so platform docs were used. Gemini 4 Carbon does not appear on the Gemini API pricing page (flagship there is Gemini 4 Argon). No Meta Llama first-party price list read.
